notes:
Top-line: Arbiter LowLatency is a mid-size algo trading platform building a low-latency inference path for real-time signal scoring and reranking. Primary goals: p95 inference latency under 30ms at 500-1,000 qps sustained; cost-per-order must be demonstrably lower than their current EC2-based endpoints. Interested in Redwood Dedicated for predictable throughput + Private for eventual on-prem deployment of sensitive order flow. Strong interest in Redwood Optimize features: batching/caching recommendations and quantization guidance.

Recent call highlights: 
- "If we can't hit 25-30ms p95 we can't deploy to production" (Head of Platform).
- Wants automatic prefix/KV caching for repeated instrument contexts (many requests share market snapshot prefixes). Prefers workload-aware batching (small batch sizes for latency tail) plus occasional burst scaling.
- Model profile: currently using a fine-tuned 7B model (proprietary head) for score/rerank; open to 4-bit quantization if Redwood Optimize shows no accuracy regression. Asked explicitly about mixed-precision options and kernel selection.
- Cost sensitivity: asked for breakouts (per-token + per-request) and scenario analysis for batching vs no-batching.

POC scope agreed: 2-week performance POC run by Redwood on dedicated test cluster using Arbiter's anonymized QPS traces. Success criteria: sustained 500 qps with p95 <30ms, 99th <50ms; memory footprint within 60% of target (to fit their reserved GPU pool); no functional regressions on scoring output (A/B QA test).

Operational/security notes:
- Must meet SOC2 controls; security team requested KMS architecture diagram and audit log retention policy.
- Data residency: order flow must remain within us-east region until legal approves cross-region replication.
- Procurement: procurement will sign once POC metrics and security questionnaire are green; expected procurement cycle ~8-10 weeks after POC.

Open technical items / asks for Redwood SE team:
- Provide perf benchmark harness + instructions to replay their recorded traces (include variability/diurnal patterns).
- Propose batching thresholds and quantization configuration options tuned for p95 latency (empirical numbers: dynamic batching max batch 16, preferred immediate cutoff 6ms).
- Provide KV/prefix cache design notes and latency impact estimates (how cache warmup behaves at startup/bursts).
- Run one controlled experiment comparing 8-bit vs 4-bit quantization for their fine-tuned model and report accuracy delta on scoring metric.

Stated blockers: security sign-off (SOC2 + KMS), clear perf validation, and legal ok on data residency. Next scheduled action: Redwood to run perf harness week of 2026-03-22; AE/SE to coordinate security follow-up concurrently.
